newsitem.title: USA: United September load factor up.
newsitem.headline: United September load factor up.

text.p: United Airlines said Thursday its systemwide passenger load factor was 71.7 percent, up from 71.1 percent a year ago.
United, which is owned by UAL Corp, said its North American passenger load factor in September rose to 68.9 percent from 66.9 percent.

Pacific load factor for the month fell to 75.1 percent from 77.7 percent, and Atlantic load factor was 87.2 percent, up from 85.6 percent. Latin American load factor was 64.3 percent in September, up from 63.5 percent.
United's total revenue passenger miles for the month rose 2.9 percent to 9.85 billion from 9.58 billion.
Available seat miles in September rose two percent to 13.74 billion from 13.47 billion.
Cargo ton miles for September rose 7.7 percent to 206.0 million from 191.3 million.

"We are particularly encouraged by our U.S. domestic traffic growth last month," John Edwardson, president, said in a statement. "Our passenger load factor for domestic markets was 68.9 percent, which was two points better than we achieved last year and about four points ahead of the industry average."
